checkpoints.name: The Harbour
checkpoints.objective: Find out why the lanterns fail.

records.title: Act I: The Coast
records.summary: The harbour lanterns guttered in the wind as the chapter opened, and the player came to the quay to learn why the lights kept failing. Arin, the harbourmaster, met them by the lamp posts and spoke plainly about the boats that could not find the channel after dark. Luke, a lamplighter, joined them and admitted that the oil stores had run low and that the old keeper had kept a ledger nobody could find. Together they searched the sheds along the water, asked the night watch what they had seen, and followed the trail of spilled oil toward the old tower. By the end of the chapter the player had earned the trust of the lamplighters, the missing ledger had been found, and the three of them stood at the foot of the tower with the last lantern still dark above them.
records.short: The player learned why the harbour lanterns failed, found the keeper's ledger and won the lamplighters' trust.

bridge.text: The chapter The Dark Harbour has ended: The player learned why the harbour lanterns failed, found the keeper's ledger and won the lamplighters' trust. A new chapter begins: The Last Lantern.

records.title: Act II: The Light
records.summary: The chapter began at the foot of the lantern tower with the wind rising off the sea. Arin and Luke led the player up the narrow stair, stopping at each landing to check the old wicks and the empty oil jars. At the top they found the great lamp cold, its glass cracked but whole enough to burn. Luke refilled the reservoir from the oil they had carried up, Arin steadied the frame against the gusts, and the player struck the light. The flame caught, the lens turned, and a beam swept across the water for the first time in weeks. Below, the boats turned toward the channel. The coast was lit again, the harbour was grateful, and the pact the three of them had sworn on the stair held.
records.short: The player relit the last lantern with Arin and Luke and the coast was lit again.

people.name: Arin
people.text: proud of the player and of the lit coast.

people.name: Luke
people.text: keeps the lamp burning and honours the pact.

records.epilogue: The wind still came off the sea, but the harbour no longer feared the dark. It had begun on a night when the lanterns guttered and the boats could not find the channel, and it had ended with a beam sweeping the water from the top of the old tower. Arin had been there from the first evening, standing by the lamp posts on the quay and speaking plainly about what the failing lights meant for the boats. Luke had come next, honest about the empty oil stores and the keeper whose ledger nobody could find. Together they searched the sheds, asked the night watch what they had seen, and followed the trail of spilled oil until the ledger was found and the lamplighters trusted the player at last. Then came the long climb. At every landing they checked the old wicks and the empty jars, and at the top they found the great lamp cold, its glass cracked but whole enough to burn. Luke filled the reservoir, Arin held the frame against the gusts, and the player struck the light. The flame caught and the lens turned. Out on the water the boats turned toward the channel, one after another, and the coast was lit again. In the weeks that followed the harbour remembered who had climbed the stair. Arin spoke of it on the quay, Luke kept the lamp burning through every storm, and the pact the three of them had sworn on the stair was never broken.
